title: TSMC CEO warns chip supply won’t meet AI-fueled demand for years
gist: TSMC CEO CC Wei told shareholders that global AI-driven chip demand will outstrip supply for years even with new US capacity, reiterating 30%+ sales growth guidance while hyperscalers are set to spend $725 billion on AI this year.

insights.claim: TSMC CEO CC Wei said global chip supply will fall short of AI-fueled demand for years to come, even as new US manufacturing capacity comes online, sustaining the company's revenue growth trajectory.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A multi-year supply shortfall thesis from the dominant foundry supports continued pricing power and margin expansion at TSMC, a bullish read for TSMC's revenue and margin trajectory.
insights.quote: It will be a long time before we can meet customer demand.
insights.locator: Even with new manufacturing capacity in the US

insights.claim: Major hyperscalers are set to spend US$725 billion on AI this year, a demand level TSMC says it cannot fully satisfy even while expanding its manufacturing footprint beyond Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A concrete $725B hyperscaler AI capex figure frames the scale of demand outstripping TSMC's leading-edge capacity, useful for sizing the AI infrastructure buildout and TSMC's addressable revenue pool.
insights.quote: major hyperscalers are set to spend US$725 billion for AI just this year
insights.locator: Taiwan's largest company is an essential player

insights.claim: TSMC reiterated guidance for sales growth of more than 30% this year, even as CEO CC Wei says the company cannot meet demand led by American customers despite expanding capacity outside Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: 30%+ revenue growth guidance combined with unmet demand suggests upside risk to consensus estimates if capacity comes online faster than expected, or continued backlog if it doesn't.
insights.quote: He reiterated its forecast for sales growth of more than 30 per cent for this year.
insights.locator: Even with new manufacturing capacity in the US

insights.claim: TSMC's capital spending is trending toward the upper end of its existing full-year forecast range of up to US$56 billion, after the company raised its full-year sales guidance in April.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Capex trending to the top of an up-to-$56B range signals TSMC is aggressively adding capacity in response to AI demand, relevant for sizing equipment supplier order flow.
insights.locator: In April, the company raised its full-year sales guidance

insights.claim: TSMC's stock fell 1% in Taipei after customer Broadcom issued a disappointing outlook, even as TSMC's own shares have more than quadrupled over the past three years.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows TSMC's stock remains sensitive to downstream customer guidance despite its own bullish supply-demand narrative, a reminder that customer-level AI capex signals can move TSMC shares short-term.
insights.quote: Shares of TSMC declined 1 per cent in Taipei after customer Broadcom provided a disappointing outlook.
insights.locator: Shares of TSMC declined 1 per cent

insights.claim: TSMC plans to raise average staff bonus payouts by more than 30% this year, a move CEO CC Wei linked to growing pressure on AI-boom winners to share more profits with employees.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Rising labor cost and profit-sharing at TSMC is a modest margin offset to watch, and signals broader pressure around AI-boom profit distribution that could recur across the supply chain.
insights.quote: TSMC staff will get more than a 30 per cent bump in their bonus payouts this year on average
